transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm just... having some trouble at work lately. I buy for a retail company, and... I don't know. I just can't shake this feeling that people at the office, and maybe some of the vendors too, are tracking my buys. Like they're messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. My supervisor showed me the reports and said they don't prove anything, but... I don't know. It just feels like it's happening.
Have you felt like people are watching or following you outside of work, or maybe even conspiring against you in other areas of your life?

No, not really outside of work. Just... like I said, it's mostly at the office. The vendors, the numbers... I just know they're messing with my buys to make me look bad. Even with the reports my supervisor showed me. It just... it feels like it's happening. That's why I'm here.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that others don't hear or see?

I... yeah, sometimes. Just... a voice. 

Like, when I'm in the stockroom alone, or... or driving back from meeting a vendor. I'll hear this guy's voice. It sounds like he's right behind me. He just says things like, "Move faster, Scott," or... or he just laughs at the buys I made. 

But when I look, there's... there's nobody there.
Besides hearing that voice, have you ever seen things or felt physical sensations that others don't seem to notice?
No... I haven't seen anything. Or felt anything weird. It's just... just the voice.
Have you ever experienced any other types of unusual perceptions, like smelling things others don’t or feeling sensations on your skin that don’t have a clear cause?
No... no, nothing like that. Just... just what I told you.
Do you ever feel like someone is putting thoughts into your mind, taking thoughts out of your mind, or that your thoughts are being broadcast for others to hear?
No. I don't... I don't think so. My thoughts are just... mine.
Have you ever had any other unusual or unshakable beliefs that others might not share or understand?

I mean... I guess there's one thing. It's actually why I agreed to come in. I just... I can't shake this feeling about work. 

I buy for a retail place, and... I just know the people there, and some of the vendors, they're... they're tracking what I buy. Like, keeping tabs on me and messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. My supervisor keeps showing me these reports, saying they don't prove anything, but... I don't know. I just know what's happening.
Can you tell me how you know that your coworkers and vendors are tracking your buys and manipulating the numbers, even though the reports don't show it?

I just... I just know. You can tell when people are watching you. The way they look at me when I walk in, or... or when an order comes up short. The reports are just... they're just paper. They can make paper say whatever they want.
Do you ever feel like your actions are being controlled by some outside force or that someone is influencing what you do without your permission?
No. Nobody is... making me do things. I'm just doing my job.
Have you ever felt that people outside of work—like strangers, family members, or friends—are also tracking your actions or trying to interfere with your life in some way?
No. Just work.
Can you explain why you continue to believe that your coworkers and vendors are tracking your buys and manipulating the numbers, even though the reports don't support this?

I don't know... it's just... that's why I came in here, honestly. I just can't shake it. Even when my supervisor sits me down and shows me the reports... I just know they're tracking my buys. The vendors, the people at work... they're messing with the launch numbers. They just want to make me look stupid. The paper doesn't matter when I can feel it happening.
Can you think of any evidence, even small things, that might convince you that your coworkers and vendors aren't actually tracking your buys and manipulating the numbers?

I don't... I don't think so. I mean, that's why I'm here. I just... I can't shake it. Even when my supervisor shows me the reports and says it's fine, it doesn't change anything. I still know they're doing it. They're tracking what I buy and messing with the numbers to make me look stupid. The reports don't... they don't prove anything to me.
Has this belief about your coworkers and vendors tracking your buys and manipulating the numbers ever gone away, even briefly, or has it stayed with you constantly since it started?
I don't really know. It's just... I guess it's always kind of there. I haven't really noticed it stopping.

Can you describe how it feels to hold this belief about your coworkers and vendors tracking your buys, even when the reports and others don't support it? Does part of you ever wonder if it might not be true?

I don't know. It's just... frustrating, I guess. Like I said, that's what really made me come in. I just can't shake the feeling. My supervisor shows me the reports, and I hear what he's saying, but... I don't know. I don't really wonder if it's not true. I just know they're tracking my buys and messing with the numbers to make me look stupid. It just feels... real.
Can you imagine any possible explanation—like a mistake or misunderstanding—that might mean your coworkers and vendors aren’t actually tracking your buys and manipulating the numbers?

I... no. Not really. I mean, I hear what you're saying about mistakes, but... that's just not it. Like I said, it's why I'm here. I just can't shake the feeling that they're tracking what I buy. The vendors, the people at work... they're messing with the launch numbers. It's to make me look stupid. Even when my supervisor shows me the reports... it doesn't matter. I just know it's happening.
